chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Attiya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"The morning (prayer time) is that which, when you see it slanting, looks like the whiteness of a shield."

As for the hadith mentioned earlier, which is the hadith of Zurara - from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: "The time of the morning prayer is between the rising of the dawn and the rising of the sun."

And what he narrated - Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab and Abdillah ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Abu Jaimah al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Sa'd ibn Tariq, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah, who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever catches one rak'ah of the morning prayer before the rising of the sun, has indeed caught the complete morning prayer."
Therefore, the meaning of these narrations is for the one with excuses and needs, as we mentioned in other prayers, and that which indicates this.
ai.seo_question: What is the defined time range for the morning prayer in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the precise temporal boundaries for Fajr prayer, distinguishing between the early time (beginning with the slanting whiteness of dawn) and the full time extending until sunrise. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that catching a single rak'ah before sunrise constitutes catching the prayer in its entirety, a ruling particularly emphasized for those with valid excuses (*ahdar*). This definition aligns with the broader scholarly consensus on the distinction between the beginning of the time (*ibtida' waqt*) and its end (*intihā' waqt*).
